entities.summary: Yasovarman I was an Angkorian king who reigned from 889 to 910 CE, earning the nickname 'Leper King' due to his physical disability. His reign was marked by power struggles with neighboring kingdoms and the construction of several temples, including the Angkor Wat temple complex. Yasovarman I's legacy includes the establishment of a stable and prosperous Angkorian Empire, which would go on to influence the region's politics and culture for centuries to come. The exact nature of his leprosy remains unclear, with some attributing it to a genetic condition and others suggesting it may have been a sign of divine favor. The impact of Yasovarman I's reign can still be seen in the architecture and art of the Angkorian Empire, which has captivated art lovers and historians alike for centuries. The legend of the 'Leper King' continues to inspire artistic interpretations and scholarly debates, cementing Yasovarman I's place in the annals of history.
